newsitem.title: IRAQ: Saddam's son escapes assassination attempt.
newsitem.headline: Saddam's son escapes assassination attempt.

text.p: The street where gunmen tried to kill President Saddam Hussein's eldest son was splattered with sheep's blood on Friday and thronged with Iraqis celebrating that Uday survived the attempt on his life.
Scores of sheep were slaughtered and the area where the assassination attempt took place was splattered in sheep's blood, a traditional sign that a bad omen was dispelled.
Thousands of people gathered at the site in Baghdad's smart district of al-Mansour, where Uday's car was attacked by gunmen as he drove through unguarded on Thursday evening.
A brass band played the national anthem, women swayed to the tune and several people showered the crowd with chocolates and other sweets.
"The evil intentions of killing the symbol of Iraq's youth (Uday) have failed," said one man. "When conspiracies fail its an occasion to celebrate," he said.
Eyewitnesses said at least two gunmen attacked Uday's car, injuring the 32-year-old along with several bystanders. Uday was reported to be in Baghdad's Ibn Sina hospital but without serious wounds.
Iraqi authorities were investigating the attempt to kill the president's son, the official media reported on Friday, wishing him a quick recovery from his wounds.
The ruling Baath party newspaper al-Thawra published the text of a presidential statement issued hours after the attack.
"Wishes for the speedy recovery of Mr Uday after being subjected to a cowardly and treacherous aggression," said al- Thawra on its front page.
No details were given of the identity of the attackers or whether there were other casualties. Investigations were under way, the paper said.
Uday used to drive without bodyguards in Baghdad and many people have reported seeing him alone or with friends dining in Baghdad restaurants.

News of the attempt on Uday's life was first broadcast on Shebab television, a popular channel he owns. A gloomy broadcaster interrupted a programme to announce that Uday was shot and wounded and taken to hospital.

"An official spokesman for the presidential office announced that Mr Uday Saddam Hussein, chairman of the Iraqi Olympic Committee, was subjected tonight to a cowardly attack during which he was wounded at 7 p.m. (1600 GMT)," the station said.
State radio and televion were broadcasting as normal on Friday and life in Baghdad went on as usual with thousands of Moslem worshippers heading for mosques to pray and listen to Friday sermons.
It was the first attempt on Uday's life reported by official Iraqi media.
Uday heads Iraq's National Olympic Committee and is also head of the Iraq Soccer Federation. He owns Iraq's most influential newspaper Babel, which does not appear on Fridays.
Uday holds a degree in engineering and military studies. He was also chairman of Iraq's Union of Journalists for two sessions.

Two years ago he supervised a national drive to repair and maintain a great number of Iraqi helicopter gunships, tanks and armoured personnel carriers. He also set up a new force known as "Saddam Commandos".
President Saddam Hussein has two sons and three daughters.
